newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland might annul Ruch sale to Hachette - paper.
newsitem.headline: Poland might annul Ruch sale to Hachette - paper.

text.p: The Polish treasury ministry, which has tentatively agreed to sell the newsstand chain Ruch SA to French Hachette Distribution Services, might annul the deal if an offer made by a domestic bidder proves better.

Deputy treasury minister Leszek Juchniewicz told the daily Gazeta Wyborcza on Thursday he might ask the minister to annul the tender and sign an agreement with a Polish consortium, Polska Grupa Kapitalowa, which includes Universal.
"I would do it without qualms," Wyborcza quoted Juchniewicz as saying. No one at the ministry was immediately available for comment.

On Thursday Universal spokeswoman Agnieszka Szostek told Reuters that her firm received a letter from the ministry asking the consortium, which includes Optimus, cable television operator Polsat and mineral water maker Multico, to make a final offer, which it would likely submit on Friday.
Last month Juchniewicz told a news conference that the ministry was seeking better terms for the deal with Hachette.
Juchniewicz said the ministry's December acceptance of a price offer of a consortium of Polish firms led by Hachette embraced only frame terms of the sale and details still needed to be hammered out.

He said he expected Hachette to spend more and sooner on increasing Ruch's capital and strongly criticised Hachette for unveiling in French and then in Polish newspapers its price offer for Ruch before a final agreement was reached.

The daily Nowa Europa last month quoted Hachette's president Jean-Louis Nachury as saying his company would pay $84 million for a 75 percent stake in Ruch and then earmark a further $45 million for increasing its capital.
Ruch has a 65 percent share of Poland's press distribution market and owns 17,000 news-stands nationwide. @
Its net profit in 1995 was 16.2 million zlotys on sales of 2.7 billion zlotys.
